Subject: Orchestrated surge SLA simulation & autoscale parameter proposal

Hi team,

Attaching the initial run of the capacity simulation for Umbra's projected q4 burst pattern (capacity-sim-results.csv) and a short draft of the autoscale rules (autoscale-rules-draft.md). High-level ask: we need a converged set of SLO-friendly autoscale parameters and a recommended burst ceiling to propose in the amendment.

What I ran into in the sim: Umbra's peak is heavily diurnal with ~10s spiky bursts for inference endpoints and sustained moderate increases for 2–3 hours. Our current baseline slab sizing hits utilization >85% during those sustained windows. The sim assumes kernel-switching and KV cache reuse (David: please confirm the cache hit assumptions).

Questions for this thread:
- David: validate the kernel-switch and prewarm assumptions and give a preferred warm-pool size (we want to avoid token-by-token cold starts).
- Karthik: propose commercial guardrails (burst multiplier, crediting, SLA credit triggers) so we can fold into the amendment.
- Umbra (Lena / procure): are there any internal constraints we need to consider for a 3rd-party-slab warm pool or prefer on-demand ephemeral handles?

Proposed timeline: finalize parameters by Fri 7/25, legal review next week, DocuSign amendment to follow.

Thanks,

Marissa — thanks for the sim. I reviewed capacity-sim-results.csv and added inline annotations (sim-annotations.txt). Notes below:

Summary of technical constraints and recommendations:
- Cache assumptions: sim uses prefix/KV cache hit rate of 62% on spikes, which is optimistic for session-less traffic. For Umbra's workload (many short chat completions), assume 45–55% unless they can surface session affinity. If we drop to 50% hit rate, CPU/GPU token cost rises ~18%.
- Warm pool: recommend a warm pool of 6–10 GPUs depending on the model family. For the sim's 200rps baseline with 2x burst, 8 GPUs gives <50ms p99 first-token on warm path.
- Prewarm window: 20–45s rolling prewarm works well; I propose default 30s for Tier-1 customers. Shorter windows reduce cold-starts but increase cost.
- Autoscale step size: 10% of slab per scale event with min step = 1 GPU and max ramp = 3 GPUs / 30s to limit noisy scaling.
- Max burst ceiling: we can technically support up to 3x baseline for short windows but recommend we cap commercial burst to 2x for committed capacity tiers to keep predictable unit economics. For ephemeral demo/POC accounts allow ephemeral 3x with throttled tokens.
- Eviction policy: weight eviction by instance age + model priority + account tier. Define explicit preemption messaging to customer on throttle events.

I've attached a formatted proposal (autoscale-proposal.pdf) with the above parameters and some sample Grafana traces. I called out where kernel switching assumptions matter (attention kernel type will change p50/p95 latency under 2x loads).

If we commit to 2x commercial burst, we should still offer a short-duration 'surge credit' bucket the customer can burn (and optionally buy top-ups). Technical side: we need a soft-eviction signal when burst bucket approaches 80%.

—David

Thanks David — very helpful annotations. A few commercial items to flag before we lock the numbers: 

1) Burst ceiling and pricing:
- We prefer to offer Umbra a Tier-1 committed slab with a 2x burst ceiling (agreed with David's technical guidance). Anything above 2x should require pre-purchased burst credits or be billed at a premium on consumption.
- Recommend we model burst credits as daily buckets that refresh; unused credits do not roll forward. We will price credits to reflect preemption and kernel-variation risk.

2) SLA credit triggers and pro-rating:
- If a customer experiences an outage during a burst window and the platform fails to scale to the agreed ceiling (2x), SLAs will be pro-rated for the portion of the window impacted. We need to define how this interacts with burst credit consumption.

3) Fallback options:
- Where possible fallback to quantized / smaller model variants during saturation (to preserve throughput) rather than hard-throttling. David: can you flag the performance/regression risk in the docs?

4) Legal / amendment path:
- I'll draft the pricing appendix and run it with legal next week. Marissa: please include a short 'ops walkthrough' schedule for Umbra's infra team so we can sign off on the fallback behaviors.

I've attached a simple commercial banding sheet so we can iterate on pricing (commercial-banding.xlsx). Rishi — pls chime if you see any billing constraints.

Karthik
Director, Commercial Ops

Lena / Umbra procurement — thanks for the quick review window. Quick recap and the decisions we're proposing for inclusion in the amendment: 

Decisions (agreed):
- Default warm-pool: 8 GPUs for the primary model family referenced in the sim.
- Prewarm window: 30s rolling window (Tier-1).
- Autoscale cadence: step size 10% / min 1 GPU / max ramp 3 GPUs per 30s.
- Commercial burst ceiling: 2x baseline for Tier-1 committed slab; Tier-2 gets 1.3x.
- Surge credit: daily burst-credit bucket for short overshoots; will be purchasable as top-ups. Soft-eviction at 80% credit consumption with a 2-minute grace period.
- Fallback path: fall back to smaller quantized model variant where possible before throttling. We will call out potential quality regressions in the amendment.

Next steps:
- I'm creating the pricing appendix and sending to legal (Karthik).
- David: please add the warm-pool and prewarm annotations to the ops playbook and include the sample Grafana traces.
- Umbra: I'll send an ops walkthrough invite for a 30-min session next week.
- DocuSign: I'll push the amendment link when legal signs off (placeholder: https://www.docusign.com/templates/umbra-ams-2028).

If that works, I'll lock the parameters and update the HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/74829/UMB-2028-0412).
